name: Betelgeuse
tagline: Orion's red shoulder — a supergiant living on borrowed time.
history: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant so vast that placed at the Sun's position it would engulf the asteroid belt. Barely ten million years old, it has already burned through its hydrogen and swollen toward death — it will collapse and explode as a supernova sometime within the next hundred thousand years, shining for weeks as bright as the Moon. Between late 2019 and early 2020 it dimmed to a third of its brightness in the 'Great Dimming', later traced by Hubble to a colossal surface eruption ejecting a dust cloud. The event proved red supergiants can lose mass violently — reshaping supernova models.
